pr_title: feat(rust): add support for `HAVING` clause to SQL `GROUP BY` operations
pr_body:
Closes #8702.

## Notes
Given the example aggregate query...
```sql
SELECT
  group,
  COUNT(DISTINCT attr) AS n_dist_attr
FROM test
GROUP BY group
```
...this PR adds support for post-aggregate HAVING clauses, such as:
```sql
HAVING n_dist_attr > 1
```
Not all SQL dialects support use of column aliases in the HAVING clause (eg: MySQL does, PostgreSQL doesn't, etc), and the ones that don't want you to re-apply the same expression that you'd find in the SELECT (due to strictness around internal evaluation order of the primary clauses), eg:
```sql
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT attr) > 1
```

The first form is definitely cleaner, but it can be argued that it's slightly less standard than the latter. Not sure if the parser allows us a way to internally map the expression back to the alias, if we wanted to try and support both? (In truth I've always much preferred the former syntax, as it seems almost self-evidently more obvious/intuitive...😅)
pr_comments: Thanks for the fix @alexander-beedie  and thanks for the review @universalmind303.

issue_context.title: HAVING clause not working as expected
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

The `HAVING` clause of SQL is not giving expected results. Ideally it should help filter the rows _after_ calculating the value of the aggregating function on each group.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

df_test = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "group": ['a', 'b', 'c', 'c', 'b'],
        "attr": ['x', 'y', 'x', 'y', 'y']
    }
)

sql_ctx = pl.SQLContext()
sql_ctx.register("test", df_test.lazy())
result = sql_ctx.execute("""
SELECT
    group,
    COUNT(DISTINCT attr) AS n_dist_attr
FROM test
GROUP BY group
HAVING n_dist_attr > 1
""")
print(result.collect())

# Output
shape: (3, 2)
┌───────┬─────────────┐
│ group ┆ n_dist_attr │
│ ---   ┆ ---         │
│ str   ┆ u32         │
╞═══════╪═════════════╡
│ a     ┆ 1           │
│ b     ┆ 1           │
│ c     ┆ 2           │
└───────┴─────────────┘
```


### Expected behavior

Ideally it should only give one row as output

```shell
shape: (1, 2)
┌───────┬─────────────┐
│ group ┆ n_dist_attr │
│ ---   ┆ ---         │
│ str   ┆ u32         │
╞═══════╪═════════════╡
│ c     ┆ 2           │
└───────┴─────────────┘
```

### Installed versions

```

Polars:      0.17.12
Index type:  UInt32
Platform:    macOS-13.3.1-x86_64-i386-64bit
Python:      3.9.15 (main, Apr 14 2023, 14:20:58) 
[Clang 14.0.3 (clang-1403.0.22.14.1)]

----Optional dependencies----

```

</details>
comments: Turns out we haven't actually implemented support for `HAVING` yet, so it's currently ignored - I'm adding it now...😅

Not sure whether this is the right thread to bring this up but would be really nice to have the following:
1. A quick query validation when the `execute` method is called. Currently that doesn't happen and it seems that query validation only happens with the `query` method.
2. A reference to the SQL dialect in the documentation expected by Polars as it throws an error if one tries to use certain common clauses like `USING` in the `JOIN` conditions or table name aliasing which are otherwise readily interpreted by other similar packages that also work with SQL such as `pyspark`, `duckdb` etc.

Thanks ! 😄
